Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

Investigation complete. Here is the factual report.

---

# PDP colour/size selection navigation — findings

## Mechanism note (affects how to read all of this)

`package.json:17-20` sets `ccExtensibility: {extends: "@salesforce/retail-react-app", overridesDir: "overrides"}`. Any file at `overrides/app/<path>` shadows `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/<path>`. Relevant consequences:

- `overrides/app/utils/url.ts` fully shadows the base `app/utils/url.js` and re-implements `productUrlBuilder`, `rebuildPathWithParams`, `updateSearchParams` itself (`overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60`, `:73`, `:199`).
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/*` all shadow their base counterparts.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx` is **not** shadowed, and still renders base `ProductTile`.

---

# QUESTION 1 — `?color=` presence on inbound PDP links

## The two URL builders

- `overrides/app/utils/url.ts:199` — `export const productUrlBuilder = (product: { id: string }): string => encodeURI(`/product/${product.id}`);` → **bare path, no query params at all.**
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:98` — identical bare path.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:35-46` / `overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60` — `rebuildPathWithParams` is the only thing that adds params, and only if a caller passes them. `updateSearchParams` (`url.js:48-57`) **deletes** a key when its value is falsy, so a `rebuildPathWithParams(url, {color: undefined})` produces **no** `color=`.

## Link sources that DO NOT carry `?color=`

| Source | file:line | href produced |
|---|---|---|
| **PLP product grid** | `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:290` — `href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }))` | `/<site>/<locale>/product/<id>` — no query string. Note `productListCardMapper.ts:286` resolves a *representative colour* for the card's images (`resolveRepresentativeColour(hit)`) but that colour is **never** put in the href. |
| PLP card wrapper | `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:745` → `:806` `<ProductListCard {...}/>` → `:229-231` spreads `cardProps` straight into `ZimmProductCard`; href untouched | unchanged |
| `ZimmProductCard` name link | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:214` `<ProductNameLink to={href}>` (`:39` `chakra(RouteLink)`) | passes through |
| `ZimmProductCard` media click | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx:605` `history.push(href)`; `:658` `<MediaOnlyCardLink to={href}>` | passes through |
| **Recently-viewed rail** (PDP/Cart/PLP) | `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts:225` — `href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }))` | no query string |
| **Recently-viewed full-history page** | `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:404` — same expression | no query string |
| **Cart / checkout / confirmation / order-detail / wishlist / order-summary / multiship line items** | `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:105` `<Link to={`/product/${productId}`}>` and `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-name.tsx:78` `to={`/product/${productId}`}`; `productId` = `variant?.master?.masterId \|\| variant.id` (`item-image.tsx:95`, `item-name.tsx:74`) | **master** id, no `color=`, no `pid=` — the specific purchased colour is discarded |
| Base wishlist primary action | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/account/wishlist/partials/wishlist-primary-action.jsx:125` and `:145` — `href={`/product/${variant.id}`}` (no override of this page exists — `overrides/app/pages/` has no `account/`) | no `color=` |
| Base "view master product" link inside ProductView | `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:1138` and `:1518` — `<Link to={`/product/${product.master.masterId}`}>` | no `color=` |
| Base search suggestions | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/search/index.jsx:80` — `link: productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId})` | no `color=`. **Not currently rendered**: the Zimmermann header uses `ZimmSearchInput` (`overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx:24`, `:258`), whose own docblock at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSearchInput/index.tsx:29` states "Suggestions UI (useSearchSuggestions popover) is Sprint 3 work". |
| Contentful / home / categoryPath / experience pages | grep for `productUrlBuilder`, `/product/`, `pdpHref`, `productHref` across `overrides/app/components/contentful/`, `overrides/app/pages/home/`, `overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/`, `overrides/app/pages/experience/` → **zero hits** | n/a |

## Link sources that DO carry `?color=`

| Source | file:line | detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Base `ProductTile`** | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx:133-139` — `rebuildPathWithParams(productUrlBuilder({id: productId}), {[selectableAttributeId]: selectableAttributeValue})`, rendered at `:186` `<Link to={productUrl}>`. `selectableAttributeId` defaults to `PRODUCT_TILE_SELECTABLE_ATTRIBUTE_ID` (`:92`) = `'color'` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:38`) | **Conditional.** `selectableAttributeValue` starts as `initialVariationValue` (`:105-111`), which is `undefined` unless the product is a master **and** has `representedProduct`. When `undefined`, `updateSearchParams` deletes the key → **no** `?color=`. |
| **Home page product scroller** | `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:17` imports base `ProductScroller`; `:104` `<ProductScroller products={productSearchResult?.hits} .../>`; reached via `HomeNormal` → `HomepageContent` (`:114`, `:155` returns `<HomepageContent />`, `:215`). `product-scroller/index.jsx:17`, `:115` render base `ProductTile`. The query at `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:47-55` uses `htype=master` + `allVariationProperties: true`. | `?color=` present when `representedProduct` resolves |
| **PDP Einstein rails** ("Complete the Set", "You might also like") | `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1348` and `:1363` render `RecommendedProducts`; `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx:132` imports base `ProductScroller` and `:548-551` renders `<ProductScroller products={recommendations.recs} ...>` → base `ProductTile` | same conditional `?color=` |
| **PDP related-colour swatches (SFCC-708)** | `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:248` — `href: `${urlBuilder({ id: item.masterProductID })}?${colourAttrId}=${encodeURIComponent(item.colourValue)}`` | **always** has `?color=`; cross-master, `forceReload: true` (`:250`) |
| PDP's own colour swatches | `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1232` (see Q3) | always |

**Note:** `RecommendedProducts` takes the `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` branch (no `?color=`) only for `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` — `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx:461-463`, documented at `:40-44`. Every other recommender falls through to the `ProductScroller`/`ProductTile` branch.

**Net answer to the "why is `urlColour` falsy" question:** the PLP grid, all recently-viewed surfaces, every cart/checkout/order/wishlist line-item link, and the master-product link inside ProductView all arrive at the PDP with **no** `color=` param. Only the home/PDP Einstein rails (via unshadowed base `ProductTile`) and PDP-internal swatches can supply one.

---

# QUESTION 2 — how `urlColour` is derived

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:324`:**

```ts
const urlColour = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID) ?? undefined;
```

- `location` is `useLocation()` (`:131`, `:223`).
- `SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` is `'color'` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:164`).
- The expression is **purely the URL read**. There is **no** fallback to a default or first-offered colour in the value of `urlColour` itself.

Two separate, distinct fallbacks exist elsewhere:

1. **Display-only fallback at the render site** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1263`: `selectedValue={urlColour ?? attr.selectedValue?.value}`. Plus `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own internal fallback: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:96` — `const effectiveSelectedValue = offered.some((v) => v.value === selectedValue) ? selectedValue : offered[0]?.value;`. Neither changes `urlColour`.

2. **A URL-writing effect that makes `urlColour` non-falsy shortly after mount** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:413-431`:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (urlColour) return;
  if (product?.id !== requestedProductId) return;
  const colourAttr = product?.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
  const defaultColourValue = (colourAttr?.values as SfccSwatchAttrValue[] | undefined)?.find(
    (v) => v.orderable !== false,
  )?.value;
  if (!defaultColourValue) return;
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  params.set(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID, defaultColourValue);
  history.replace(`${location.pathname}?${params.toString()}`);
}, [urlColour, product, requestedProductId]);
```
So on a `?color=`-less arrival, `urlColour` is `undefined` for the first render(s) — until `product.id === requestedProductId` and a first orderable colour value exists — then a `history.replace` writes `?color=<first orderable>` and `urlColour` becomes truthy on the next render. It stays `undefined` forever if `defaultColourValue` is falsy (`:427`).

Also consumed at `:459` and `:464` by `selectVariantScopedPriceData` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts:92`, `:113-117`).

---

# QUESTION 3 — colour swatch navigation mechanism

## Component location

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:74` (`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`), atom at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:71` (`ZimmColourSwatch`).

Two call sites:
1. PDP main sidebar — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1257`
2. Gallery overlay "Also available in" — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:218`

## How swatch `href` values are generated

### (a) PDP main sidebar — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1221-1235`

```ts
const values = (attr.values ?? []).map((v: SfccSwatchAttrValue) => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  params.delete('pid');
  params.set(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID, v.value ?? '');
  return {
    value: v.value ?? '',
    name: v.name ?? v.value ?? '',
    imageUrl: v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link,
    href: `${location.pathname}?${params.toString()}`,
    orderable: v.orderable ?? true,
  };
});
```

**Param handling:** same pathname; **`pid` is explicitly deleted** (`:1226`, rationale at `:1223-1225`); `color` is set; **every other existing param — including `size` — is preserved verbatim.**

Note: the Zimmermann size selector does *not* write `size` into the URL — `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:465-483` keeps the picked size in local `localSizeValue` state (comment at `:466-468`: "size must not change the URL"), and `setLocalSizeValue` is called only at `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:1290`. So a `size=` param is normally absent; if it is present (e.g. a base-built deep link), it survives the colour swap.

### (b) Related-colour swatches (SFCC-708), appended to the same group — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1243-1252` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:239-251`

```ts
href: `${urlBuilder({ id: item.masterProductID })}?${colourAttrId}=${encodeURIComponent(item.colourValue)}`,
orderable: true as const,
forceReload: true as const,
```
`urlBuilder` = `(params) => buildHref(productUrlBuilder(params))` (`index.tsx:1249`). This is a **fresh** URL: it **drops every existing param**, including `pid` and `size`.

### (c) Gallery overlay swatches — `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:520-539`

```ts
const naturalColourValues = colourAttr?.values.map((v) => ({ ..., href: v.href, ... })) ?? [];
```
`href: v.href` (`:527`) comes from base `useVariationAttributes`. Two sub-cases:
- **Uncontrolled** (no size picked yet): `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js:152-161` → `buildVariantValueHref` (`:45-63`), which does `updateSearchParams(allParams, newParams)` on `usePDPSearchParams`'s `allParams` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-pdp-search-params.js:12`). This **preserves `pid`** — it only sets the variation-attribute keys. That is the opposite of the main sidebar's `params.delete('pid')`.
- **Controlled** (a size has been picked → `effectiveControlledVariationValues !== null`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:471-483`, passed at `:507`): `use-variation-attributes.js:152-153` returns `href: null`. The overlay passes no `onSelect` (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:218-225`), so `ZimmColourSwatch` falls to the linkless `<chakra.button>` branch (`zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:155-170`) with `onClick={undefined}` (`zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:255`: `onClick={onSelect ? () => onSelect(v.value) : undefined}`) — i.e. **a dead swatch**. Flagging as an observation; not one of the four questions.

## Link vs. full navigation

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx`:

- `:11` — `const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink);` where `RouteLink` is `Link as RouteLink` from `react-router-dom` (`:3`).
- `:109-133` — **if `href && forceReload`** → plain `<chakra.a href={href}>` (`:112`), and Space key does `window.location.href = href` (`:126`). **Full document navigation / full remount.** This branch is taken only by the SFCC-708 related-colour swatches.
- `:135-151` — **else if `href`** → `<ColourSwatchLink to={href}>` (`:137-138`). **react-router `<Link>` → client-side `history.push`, no document reload, no route unmount.** This is the branch every same-master colour swatch takes.
- `:155-170` — no `href` → `<chakra.button onClick={onClick}>`, no navigation.

Keyboard arrow navigation in the group mirrors this exactly — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:145` `const history = useHistory();`, `:170-175`:
```ts
if (next.href) {
  if (next.forceReload) { window.location.href = next.href; }
  else { history.push(next.href); }
} else { onSelect?.(next.value); }
```

## Base comparison

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/swatch.jsx:60-61` — `as={href ? RouteLink : 'button'}` / `to={href}`. Same client-side `Link` approach; no `forceReload` concept.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx:682-749` — renders `<Swatch href={href} .../>` inside `<SwatchGroup>` from the `variationAttributes` array; hrefs come from `useVariationAttributes`, i.e. all params preserved including `pid`.
- Zimmermann's `ProductView` keeps that base `SwatchGroup` path for non-colour attributes (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:1369-1429`) and lets the PDP inject `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` for `color` via `renderVariationAttribute` (`:1256` `const custom = renderVariationAttribute?.(attr);`, contract documented at `:278-283`).
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:218-239` (`getDecoratedVariationAttributes`, used by base `ProductTile`) builds `href: rebuildPathWithParams(productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId}), variationValues)` — a fresh path plus only the variation values.

---

# QUESTION 4 — does changing colour remount `ProductView`?

## No `key` on `<ProductView>`

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1212-1318` — the standard-product `<ProductView ... />`. Its full prop list (read at `1212-1318`) contains **no `key=` prop**. The set/bundle parent instance at `:1118` likewise has none; the per-child instance at `:1144` is keyed on the enclosing `<Box key={childProduct.id}>` (`:1143`) — a product id, not the colour.

`ProductView` is a module-level `forwardRef` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:379`, `:1683`, exported at `:1692`) — stable element type across renders, and not wrapped in `React.memo`.

The only `key`s in the PDP render path that move on navigation are:
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1381` — `key={location.key}` on the **"Recently Viewed" `RecommendedProducts`** rail only (comment at `:1379-1380`). This *does* remount on every colour click, but it is a sibling of `ProductView`, not an ancestor.
- `:1321` — `key={activePdpTabId ?? 'closed'}` on `ZimmPdpDrawer`.
- `:1094` — `key={id}` on `<meta>` tags.

`<Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>` (`:1211`) is a pass-through wrapper (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/island/index.jsx:86-90`) and adds no key.

## Route behaviour on a query-string-only change

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:75-78`:
```ts
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,
},
```
react-router v5 matches on `pathname` only; `location.search` is not part of the path match. A colour swatch `history.push` changes only the search string, so the same `<Route>` stays matched with the same `component` reference (`ProductDetail`, a `loadable` created once at module scope) — **the route does not unmount**. The component re-renders with a new `location` object.

Supporting evidence that the codebase relies on exactly this: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:284-297` sets `keepPreviousData: true` on `useProduct` with an explicit comment that `ZimmProductContent` "never unmounts on a variant change, so the price element survives and React mutates its text in place" for the `aria-live` announcement. A remount would defeat that.

## Conclusion

On a colour query-param change the `ProductView` subtree is **re-rendered, not remounted**. Nothing in the render path changes the React element identity or key of `<ProductView>` when `?color=` changes — no `key`, no conditional element type, no wrapper keyed on location, and no route unmount.

**Direct behavioural consequence worth noting:** because `ProductView` is not remounted, its `localSizeValue` state (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:469`) survives a colour change. `setLocalSizeValue` is called at exactly one place — `:1290`, the size selector's `onSelectionChange` — and there is no reset effect (the only location/variation-keyed effect in the file is `:1017-1021`, which merely calls `toggleShowOptionsMessage(false)`). So a previously selected size stays selected across a colour swap, and `effectiveControlledVariationValues` (`:471-483`) stays non-null, which in turn keeps `useVariationAttributes` in controlled mode and keeps `v.href === null` for the gallery-overlay swatches (see Q3c).

---

## Things I could not determine

1. **Whether base `ProductTile`'s `?color=` actually materialises at runtime on the home page and the PDP Einstein rails.** It depends on `product.representedProduct` being populated in the SFCC/Einstein response (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx:104-111`). Static reading cannot settle it; the home query does request `allVariationProperties: true` and `htype=master` (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:47-55`), which makes it likely there, and Einstein recs (`overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx:548-551`) are hydrated via `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` whose merged shape I did not verify field-by-field for `representedProduct`. Needs a live check.
2. **Whether any Contentful-authored CTA in the CMS points at `/product/...?color=`.** Contentful hrefs are data, not code; grep over `overrides/app/components/contentful/`, `overrides/app/pages/home/`, `overrides/app/pages/experience/`, `overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/` for `productUrlBuilder`, `/product/`, `pdpHref`, `productHref` returned zero hits, so no *code* path builds one.
3. I searched for the colour param under `color`, `colour`, `Color`, `Colour`, `SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID`, `PRODUCT_TILE_SELECTABLE_ATTRIBUTE_ID`, `urlColour`/`urlColor`, and for link generation under `productUrlBuilder`, `rebuildPathWithParams`, `buildVariantValueHref`, `updateSearchParams`, `/product/` literals, `to={`/`href={` with product targets, `ProductTile`, `product-scroller`, `item-variant`, and every `select*Card` mapper. I believe the Q1 enumeration is exhaustive for code-generated PDP links.
